overall: The AG found no Open Meeting Law violation: the Council's April 22, 2025 review of the 2017 executive session minutes was timely because the records request was not an OML minutes request. The AG declined to rule on the attorney-client privilege withholding.

allegations.summary: Complainant alleged the Council failed to timely review and release February 21, 2017 executive session minutes after a March 13, 2025 records request.
allegations.key_passage: Therefore, the Council did not violate the Open Meeting Law when it reviewed the requested executive session minutes during its meeting on April 22, 2025, which was the fourth meeting following the request.

allegations.summary: Council withheld the 2017 executive session minutes under attorney-client privilege; the complaint challenged that withholding.
allegations.key_passage: The Open Meeting Law authorizes the Attorney General to investigate a complaint alleging a violation of the Open Meeting Law and to request documents in the course of that investigation but does not give the Division the authority to determine whether the Council's assertion of the attorney-client privilege or any other exemption under the Public Records Law is justified.
